run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:18:42Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by frontend-proxy generating HTTP 504s for POST /api/checkout: its access log shows '504 UT response_timeout ... 15000' (Envoy upstream response timeout of 15 s), while the same requests take ~30 s end-to-end. The trace chain shows the extra time is spent in checkout: checkout's server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder runs ~30.1 s because its HTTP POST call to the email Service (ClusterIP 100.67.49.77, port 8080) ends with the error 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' after 30.0 s. Email's own application spans show no errors and no spans slower than 1 s, its two pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and are present in the email Endpoints, so the email service is up but unreachable at the network level from checkout (a subset of connections still gets through, and email's received request rate fell from ~242/5m to ~30-58/5m per pod). PodNetworkChaos resources for the checkout pod and both email pods are the only cluster-level events that start with the incident (18:18:32, repeating through 18:25:32), and no pod restarted. The exact alert expression and the reported 0.2444 value could not be reproduced because no RequestErrorRate rule is present in this Prometheus, and the chaos resources themselves cannot be read with the available resource kinds.

claims.text: At 18:20:00 frontend-proxy span metrics recorded STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.0852 spans/s against STATUS_CODE_UNSET at 23.88 spans/s, so the service was emitting error spans, matching the alert's 'error rate above 0' claim.

The frontend-proxy error spans are exclusively the server operation 'ingress' (increase of 25.6 then 123.3 then 94.6 error spans per 5m from 18:20 onwards); the client operation 'router frontend egress' shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 at every bin even though its spans carry error="true"/http.status_code="0".

The frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 errors started in the 18:18-18:20 window: the per-2m increase went from 0-4 before 18:18 to 29.3 in the 18:18-18:20 bucket, then stayed between 46.7 and 72 per 2m until 18:34, i.e. the error burst begins at the alert's start time and persists.

frontend-proxy's own access log contains lines of the form '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout - "-" ... 15000' (178 such lines in the log segment read, 18:18:00-18:26:22), i.e. the proxy returned 504 because the upstream did not respond within a 15000 ms response timeout; all 10 newest matching lines are POST /api/checkout.

In trace 98e909febe9b71752501a3fe3cbf3ed0 the parent-child chain is: load-generator POST (15.00 s, http.status_code 504, error) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (15.00 s, 504, ERROR) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (15.00 s) -> frontend 'POST' 15.00 s (http.status_code 200) and 'POST /api/checkout' 30.19 s -> frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 30.19 s -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 30.12 s -> checkout 'HTTP POST' 30.00 s with error detail 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'.

In trace b714723a5df7a555e9d08895ca0a8814 the frontend 'POST' span lasted 15,001,621 us and recorded http.status_code 200, while its children were fast (checkout prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart 7.1 ms, CartService/GetCart 0.8 ms, CurrencyService/Convert 1.8 ms, PaymentService/Charge 78 ms, shipping /get-quote 2.0 ms and /ship-order 0.1 ms), showing the extra time is not in those downstream calls.

The checkout PlaceOrder duration histogram for 18:25-18:30 shows 129.4 spans in le="+Inf" but only 37.3 in le="15000.0" and 28.6 in le="10000.0", so about 92 PlaceOrder spans in that 5m window exceeded 15 s; the PlaceOrder increase with duration over 1 s was 157.8 per 5m in the same period.

Across the whole incident window 18:18:42-18:36:42, spans longer than 5 s were counted only for checkout (501.9), frontend (1032.4), frontend-proxy (517.8), accounting (17.9) and one span each for recommendation, ad and fraud-detection (1.05 each); cart, currency, email, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote and shipping had none.

Error spans in 18:18:42-18:36:42 were recorded by frontend-proxy (218.9), checkout (100.9) and by exactly one span each on recommendation, ad and fraud-detection (1.05); of the 15 services reporting span metrics, cart, currency, email, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote and shipping recorded no error spans.

The dial-timeout destination 100.67.49.77 is the ClusterIP of the 'email' Service in otel-demo with port 8080/targetPort 8080, and that Service's Endpoints contain both email pods (100.96.2.7 = email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn, 100.96.3.218 = email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w).

The email pods email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w (100.96.3.218) and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn (100.96.2.7), and the checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy pods, are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-16T17:45:2x, i.e. none of them crashed or restarted during the incident.

The email application itself shows no failure: its operation-level spans over 1 s (POST /send_order_confirmation, send_email, sinatra.render_template) are 0 at every 5m bin, while the number of POST /send_order_confirmation spans received fell from 242.2 per 5m at the 18:15 bin to 113.3 at 18:25 and 77.2 at 18:30.

Both email pods still served POST /send_order_confirmation during 18:25-18:35 but at reduced rates seen through exported_instance: email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w (uid 3fb61602-10bf-4c1b-852c-d65334a985eb) went 141.1 -> 57.8 -> 29.9 per 5m and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn (uid 6a3edbee-fe4a-40ce-9e58-1591f36a2ad1) went 5.6 -> 55.6 -> 47.3 per 5m.

The only cluster events that coincide with the onset are 'Updated' events for PodNetworkChaos objects checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn, repeating every 30-60 s from 2026-11-16T18:18:32Z through 18:25:32Z.

frontend-proxy kept serving other routes normally during the incident: its log shows 'GET /api/cart', 'GET /api/products/...', 'GET /api/recommendations...' and 'POST /api/cart' returning 200 via_upstream up to 18:26:22.

Most likely cause: a network-level disruption injected between the checkout and email pods (PodNetworkChaos objects exist on checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs and both email pods and are the only change coinciding with the onset) blackholes or delays checkout's TCP connects to the email Service VIP 100.67.49.77:8080, so PlaceOrder waits out the 30 s dial timeout; frontend's POST /api/checkout then exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream response timeout, producing the 504 error spans that raise RequestErrorRate for frontend-proxy. The exact chaos parameters (loss vs delay vs partition, direction) cannot be read with the available resource kinds, so the mechanism beyond 'TCP connect to email times out' is not confirmed.

The disruption impairs rather than fully severs the checkout-to-email path: both email pods continued to receive POST /send_order_confirmation at reduced rates while many other attempts ended in 30 s dial timeouts, which is more consistent with packet loss/delay or a partial policy than with a complete partition; whether the policy is applied on the checkout (egress) side or the email (ingress) side cannot be distinguished from the evidence.

The email Service was not without endpoints and email was not resource-sick: both email pods are listed in the Endpoints for port 8080, are Ready with 0 restarts, and recorded no span over 1 s. This rules out 'no endpoints / pod down / slow email application' as the explanation for the i/o timeout and points to reachability rather than to the email process.

frontend did not report an application error: its 'POST /api/checkout' span completed with http.status_code 200 after 30.19 s while frontend-proxy logged '504 UT response_timeout' at 15 s, i.e. the 504 is the proxy's upstream timeout firing before the application finished, not a 5xx emitted by frontend.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself failing or restarting. Its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, it kept returning 200 via_upstream for /api/cart, /api/products and /api/recommendations, and its 504s carry the Envoy 'UT response_timeout' flag with a 15000 ms upstream timeout, i.e. the proxy is functioning and timing out on a slow upstream.

Rejected: errors in the other backends (payment, cart, currency, shipping, quote, product-catalog, image-provider, email). In 18:18:42-18:36:42 those services recorded no error spans and no spans longer than 5 s, and the individual calls inside the failing traces (GetCart, CurrencyService/Convert, PaymentService/Charge, shipping /get-quote and /ship-order, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct) completed in milliseconds or tens of milliseconds.

Rejected as a cause of this incident: the slow accounting 'order-consumed' spans. Spans over 5 s on that operation already occurred before the onset (6.77 in 18:03-18:08, 3.33 in 18:13-18:18, 7.78 in 18:23-18:28), so they are pre-existing background behaviour rather than a consequence of, or contributor to, the 504 burst.

gaps: The chaos resources could not be read: 'podnetworkchaos' (and NetworkChaos) is not an allowed resource kind here, so the experiment name, its loss/delay/partition parameters, direction (checkout egress vs email ingress) and its lifetime remain unknown; only the PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events are visible.

No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate is loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the exact expression behind the alert and its reported value 0.2444444444444444 could not be reproduced or checked.

Application logs for the frontend pod (frontend-675fd7b5c5-kzdpp) and the email pod (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w) returned no lines for 18:20-18:36, so no application-side confirmation of the delay or of the dropped connections is available.
Kubernetes events for the PodNetworkChaos objects were returned only up to 2026-11-16T18:25:32Z, so whether the chaos resources remained active after that point is unknown.

The query kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="otel-demo",deployment=~"email|checkout|frontend|frontend-proxy"} returned no series, so deployment-level ready-replica counts could not be verified (pod-level status was verified instead).
Node-level and CNI/network metrics were not examined, so the packet-level mechanism and whether a node-level issue contributed are unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment/config/chaos-schedule history could be compared with the onset.

The one-off error spans counted on recommendation ('/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream'), ad and fraud-detection (1.05 each over 18 minutes) were not investigated and there is no evidence tying them to this incident.
next_steps: Inspect the NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos experiment that targets checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn (parameters, direction, duration, creation time) and confirm that removing it stops the 504s.

Compare the client dial timeout used by checkout to the email Service (observed 30 s) with frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout for /api/checkout, and confirm the 15 s value is intentional routing configuration.
Check whether the email Service ClusterIP dial failures also affect any other client of email, using per-client network metrics or node-level packet-drop counters if available.
Load the alerting rule that computes RequestErrorRate for frontend-proxy to confirm which metric and denominator produce the reported 0.2444 value.
